items.prompt: Which structure is found in bacterial cells but not in animal cells?

options.label: Mitochondria
Peptidoglycan cell wall
Golgi apparatus
Membrane-bound nucleus

rubric: Peptidoglycan is a cell wall component unique to bacteria.
Distractors are eukaryotic organelles that bacteria lack.

items.prompt: What colour do Gram-positive bacteria appear after a standard Gram stain?

options.label: Green
Pink
Purple
Colourless

rubric: Gram-positive cells keep the crystal violet and look purple.
Pink is the Gram-negative result, the most common mix-up.

items.prompt: Which term names the usual way a bacterial cell reproduces?

options.label: Sporulation
Mitosis
Meiosis
Binary fission

rubric: Bacteria divide by binary fission into two cells.
Mitosis and meiosis occur in eukaryotes; sporulation is survival, not reproduction.

items.prompt: What is a virus that infects bacteria called?

options.label: Bacteriophage
Prion
Protozoan
Mycelium

rubric: A bacteriophage is a virus that infects bacteria.
Prions are infectious proteins, not viruses; the others are not viruses at all.

items.prompt: Which substance is the main component of fungal cell walls?

options.label: Peptidoglycan
Lipopolysaccharide
Cellulose
Chitin

rubric: Fungal walls contain chitin.
Peptidoglycan is bacterial and cellulose is found in plants.

items.prompt: Which of the following organisms are prokaryotes? Select all that apply.

options.label: Saccharomyces cerevisiae
Staphylococcus aureus
Escherichia coli
Plasmodium falciparum

rubric: E. coli and S. aureus are bacteria, which are prokaryotes.
Yeast is a fungus and Plasmodium is a protozoan, both eukaryotes.

items.prompt: A laboratory technician must sterilise heat-stable glassware and culture media before an experiment. The technician uses an autoclave and needs to recall the standard setting. Which setting is the standard for autoclave sterilisation?

options.label: 72 °C at normal pressure held for 30 minutes
121 °C under steam pressure for 15 to 20 minutes
100 °C boiling at normal pressure for 30 minutes
37 °C at normal pressure held for 24 hours

rubric: Standard autoclaving is 121 °C at about 15 psi for 15 to 20 minutes.
Lower temperatures or boiling at normal pressure do not reliably destroy endospores.

items.prompt: Why are antibiotics such as penicillin ineffective against viral infections?

options.label: Viruses mutate so quickly that the drug is broken down before it can act
Viruses are too small for the drug to reach them inside the host cell
Viruses have no cell wall or own metabolism for the drug to target
Viruses replicate only inside the nucleus, where the drug cannot enter

rubric: Penicillin blocks cell wall synthesis, and viruses have no wall or independent metabolism.
Size or location explanations ignore the missing drug target.

items.prompt: Why are Gram-negative bacteria often harder to treat with some antibiotics than Gram-positive bacteria?

options.label: They have no cell wall at all
They contain a nucleus that shields the DNA
They reproduce much faster than Gram-positive cells
They have an outer membrane that limits drug entry

rubric: The outer membrane acts as a barrier to many drugs.
Gram-negative bacteria do have a thin wall and no nucleus.

items.prompt: How do moulds differ from yeasts?

options.label: Moulds are prokaryotes with no nucleus, while yeasts are eukaryotes with one
Moulds cannot reproduce by spores, so they spread only by cell division, unlike yeasts
Moulds grow as filaments called hyphae; yeasts are mostly single cells
Moulds are bacteria that form branching colonies, while yeasts are true fungi

rubric: Moulds are multicellular filamentous fungi; yeasts are unicellular fungi.
Both are eukaryotic fungi and moulds do make spores.

items.prompt: A bacterium divides every 20 minutes under ideal conditions. If a culture starts with 100 cells, how many cells are expected after 60 minutes?
rubric: Three doublings give 100 x 2^3 = 800.
300 and 600 add rather than double; 1000 assumes ten-fold growth.

items.prompt: Why can bacterial endospores survive boiling water when ordinary cells cannot?

options.label: They make heat-shock proteins that refold damaged enzymes quickly
They are dormant, dry structures with tough coats
They keep dividing quickly to replace killed cells
They contain extra DNA copies that repair heat damage

rubric: Endospores are dormant, dry and heavily coated, so they resist heat.
Distractors imply active growth or repair, but spores are metabolically inactive.

items.prompt: Which statements correctly explain why refrigeration slows food spoilage? Select all that apply.

options.label: Most spoilage microbes grow more slowly at cold temperatures
Cold temperatures kill all bacteria in the food
Low temperature slows the enzyme reactions microbes need
Cold air removes water from the food

rubric: Cold slows enzyme activity and thus microbial growth.
Refrigeration is bacteriostatic, not sterilising, and does not dry food.

items.prompt: A student spreads bacteria on an agar plate and places a paper disc soaked in an antibiotic on it. After overnight incubation, a clear ring with no growth surrounds the disc, while bacteria grow thickly elsewhere. What does the clear ring indicate?

options.label: The agar under the disc has dried out and cannot support growth
The bacteria are resistant and have moved away from the disc
The drug killed only dead cells, so the bacteria are tolerant to it
The drug stopped growth, so the bacteria are susceptible to it

rubric: A zone of inhibition means the drug stopped growth, showing susceptibility.
Resistant bacteria would grow right up to the disc.

items.prompt: Why do Gram-positive bacteria stay purple after the alcohol decolorising step of a Gram stain?

options.label: Their thin peptidoglycan layer binds safranin more tightly than it binds crystal violet
Their thick peptidoglycan layer holds the crystal violet-iodine complex after decolorising
Their outer membrane of lipopolysaccharide traps the crystal violet after the alcohol wash
Their missing cell wall lets the dye bind DNA more strongly than the counterstain

rubric: A thick peptidoglycan wall dehydrates and retains the crystal violet-iodine complex.
The outer membrane distractor describes Gram-negative cells, which lose the stain.

items.prompt: Which statement best explains why viruses are not classed as living cells?

options.label: They hold only RNA, which cells cannot use to pass on inherited information to offspring
They lack their own metabolism and can only replicate using a host cell's machinery
They have no proteins, so they cannot build any protective structure around their genome
They are smaller than ribosomes, so they cannot carry any genes of their own at all

rubric: Viruses lack independent metabolism and depend on host machinery to replicate.
Distractors wrongly claim viruses lack proteins or that RNA cannot be genetic material.

items.prompt: A culture is moved into fresh medium. For a while the cell number barely rises while cells make enzymes and adjust. Which growth phase is this?

options.label: Log phase
Stationary phase
Death phase
Lag phase

rubric: The lag phase is adaptation with little division.
Log phase is a common confusion, but there cells divide at their fastest.

items.prompt: After incubation in thioglycolate broth, bacteria grow only in a dense band at the very top of the tube. What does this indicate about the organism?

options.label: It is an obligate anaerobe, because oxygen at the top of the tube is toxic to it
It is an aerotolerant anaerobe, because it ignores oxygen and grows at any depth in the tube
It is a facultative anaerobe, because it grows evenly throughout the whole tube regardless of oxygen
It is an obligate aerobe, because it needs oxygen for respiration and so stays at the top

rubric: Growth only where oxygen is highest indicates an obligate aerobe.
Anaerobes would grow at the bottom; facultative organisms would grow throughout the tube.

items.prompt: Penicillin kills growing bacteria but is generally safe for human cells. Which explanation is best?

options.label: It blocks cross-linking of peptidoglycan, which human cells do not have in their walls
It dissolves the nucleus, and bacteria have a nucleus that is more exposed than ours
It binds to cholesterol in membranes, which is present in bacteria but not in human cells
It destroys 80S ribosomes, which are found only in bacterial cells and not in human cells

rubric: Penicillin inhibits peptidoglycan cross-linking, a bacteria-specific structure.
Ribosome and cholesterol distractors invert real facts: bacteria have 70S ribosomes and generally lack cholesterol.

items.prompt: Which of the following are typical features of bacterial (prokaryotic) cells? Select all that apply.

options.label: A single, usually circular chromosome
70S ribosomes
80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm
Mitochondria for ATP production
No membrane-bound nucleus

rubric: Bacteria lack a nucleus, have 70S ribosomes and usually one circular chromosome.
Mitochondria and 80S ribosomes are eukaryotic features.

items.prompt: In a disk diffusion test, a lawn of bacteria is spread on an agar plate. Disk A shows a clear 22 mm zone around it. Disk B, a different antibiotic, shows no clear zone, and bacteria grow right up to the disk. How should the result be interpreted?

options.label: The bacteria are likely resistant to antibiotic A and likely susceptible to antibiotic B
The bacteria are susceptible to both, since both disks were placed on the same plate
The bacteria are likely susceptible to antibiotic A and likely resistant to antibiotic B
The bacteria are resistant to both, since a clear zone means the antibiotic failed to diffuse

rubric: A clear zone means growth was inhibited, while growth up to the disk suggests resistance.
Reversing the meaning of the zone is the typical misconception.

items.prompt: A culture is diluted 1:10 three times in a row (a total dilution of 10^-3). Then 0.1 mL of the last tube is plated and gives 45 colonies. What is the original concentration in CFU/mL?
rubric: Other options come from forgetting the 0.1 mL plating volume or misusing the dilution factor.

items.prompt: A culture starts with 100 bacterial cells and has a generation time of 30 minutes. Assuming continuous exponential growth with no lag, how many cells are there after 2 hours?
rubric: 2 hours is 4 generations, so 100 x 2^4 = 1600.
800 comes from counting 3 doublings; 400 from treating growth as linear.

items.prompt: Which setting should be chosen to reliably sterilise a flask of contaminated heat-stable broth, including bacterial endospores, in an autoclave?

options.label: 121 °C at about 15 psi for 15 to 20 minutes
60 °C for 30 minutes, which is gentle and kills all vegetative cells
100 °C in boiling water for 10 minutes at normal pressure
72 °C for 15 seconds, which kills most pathogens quickly

rubric: Pressurised steam at 121 °C for 15-20 minutes destroys endospores.
Boiling and pasteurisation-type conditions do not reliably kill endospores.

items.prompt: A technician Gram-stains a smear and sees pink rod-shaped cells under the microscope. How should the organism be classified?

options.label: Gram-negative rods, because they lost crystal violet and took up safranin
Gram-positive rods, because rods retain the crystal violet
Gram-negative cocci, because pink cells have lost the cell wall
Gram-positive cocci, because pink indicates the counterstain was taken up

rubric: Pink cells decolorised and took up safranin, so they are Gram-negative; shape is rod.
Confusing colour with shape or wall presence leads to the other options.

items.prompt: A bacterial isolate forms pink colonies on MacConkey agar. Which conclusion follows?

options.label: It is an obligate anaerobe, because pink colour comes from lack of oxygen use
It is a Gram-positive coccus, because pink colonies show the thick wall took up dye
It cannot ferment lactose, and it is inhibited by bile salts and crystal violet
It ferments lactose, and it grows in the presence of bile salts and crystal violet

rubric: MacConkey is selective for bile-tolerant (mostly Gram-negative) bacteria and shows lactose fermenters as pink.
Gram-positive cocci are inhibited on this medium, and colony colour does not reflect oxygen needs.

items.prompt: A hospital must sterilise heat-sensitive plastic instruments that would melt in an autoclave. Which methods are suitable? Select all that apply.

options.label: Hydrogen peroxide gas plasma
Autoclaving at 121 °C
Dry heat at 160 °C for 2 hours
Ethylene oxide gas
Gamma irradiation

rubric: Ethylene oxide, gamma irradiation and gas plasma sterilise without high heat.
Autoclaving and dry heat would melt or damage the plastic.

items.prompt: A clinical lab examines a wound swab isolate. It is a Gram-positive coccus in clusters, catalase-positive and coagulase-positive. Applying the standard identification scheme, which organism is the most likely?

options.label: Streptococcus pyogenes
Enterococcus faecalis
Staphylococcus aureus
Staphylococcus epidermidis

rubric: Gram-positive clusters that are catalase-positive point to Staphylococcus, and coagulase-positive identifies S. aureus.
S. epidermidis is coagulase-negative; streptococci and enterococci are catalase-negative.

items.prompt: 1 mL of a broth culture is diluted 1:10 three successive times (total dilution 10^-3). 0.1 mL of the final dilution is spread on agar and gives 45 colonies. What is the original concentration?

options.label: 4.5 x 10^4 CFU/mL
4.5 x 10^3 CFU/mL
4.5 x 10^6 CFU/mL
4.5 x 10^5 CFU/mL

rubric: Distractors come from ignoring the 0.1 mL plated volume or miscounting the dilution factor.

items.prompt: A culture grows exponentially with no lag from 1,000 cells/mL to 64,000 cells/mL in 3 hours. What is its generation time?

options.label: 20 minutes
30 minutes
60 minutes
45 minutes

rubric: 64,000/1,000 = 64 = 2^6, so 6 doublings in 180 minutes gives 30 minutes.
Distractors come from miscounting doublings or dividing by the fold increase.

items.prompt: A technician forgets the alcohol decolorizer when Gram staining a smear of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. How will the cells appear?

options.label: Both colourless, because without the decolorizer no stain can bind to either cell wall type
Both pink, because safranin overpowers the crystal violet in every cell type on the slide
E. coli pink and S. aureus purple, because wall structure alone decides the colour regardless of the steps
Both purple, because the crystal violet-iodine complex was never washed out of the gram-negative cells

rubric: Decolorizer is what removes the dye complex from gram-negative cells; without it all cells stay purple.
Distractors assume the normal result or that the counterstain dominates.

items.prompt: You must sterilize 200 mL of a heat-labile antibiotic solution before adding it to cooled agar. Which method fits best?

options.label: Boiling for 10 minutes, since that kills all vegetative bacterial cells in the solution
Autoclaving at 121°C for 15 minutes, since that reliably destroys even bacterial endospores
Filtering through a 0.22 µm membrane, since that removes bacteria and fungi without heat
Exposing it to UV light for 30 minutes, since that penetrates the whole volume evenly

rubric: Membrane filtration removes microbes without heat damage to the antibiotic.
Boiling and autoclaving degrade the drug; UV penetrates liquids poorly.

items.prompt: A colony is colourless on MacConkey agar (bile salts, crystal violet, lactose, neutral red). What can you conclude?

options.label: It is Gram-positive, because bile salts and crystal violet allow only those cells to grow
It does not ferment lactose, but it tolerates bile salts and crystal violet well enough to grow
It is inhibited, because colourless colonies mean the medium suppressed its growth completely
It ferments lactose, because colourless colonies indicate acid production from the sugar

rubric: Growth shows bile tolerance (typically gram-negative); no pink means no lactose fermentation acidifying the medium.
Distractors reverse the colour logic or the selective action.

items.prompt: You need to culture a strict anaerobe from a wound sample. Which measures are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.label: Inoculate thioglycolate broth, which contains a reducing agent
Grow it in a shaking flask for maximum aeration
Incubate plates in an anaerobic jar with a gas-generating pack
Use pre-reduced media with a resazurin oxygen indicator
Incubate in a candle jar to lower oxygen

rubric: Anaerobic jars, reducing media and indicators remove or monitor oxygen.
Candle jars give a CO2-enriched atmosphere that still has oxygen; shaking adds oxygen.

items.prompt: A lab runs a broth MIC test for ampicillin against an isolate. Tubes contain 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 µg/mL. After 18 hours, the tubes at 2, 4 and 8 µg/mL are turbid, and those at 16 and 32 µg/mL are clear. What is the MIC?

options.label: 4 µg/mL
32 µg/mL
8 µg/mL
16 µg/mL

rubric: The MIC is the lowest concentration with no visible growth: 16 µg/mL.
Distractors choose the highest turbid tube, the highest tested, or a lower one.

items.prompt: After incubation, an uninoculated control broth tube is turbid, as are all the test tubes. Which interpretation is best?

options.label: The medium or aseptic technique was contaminated, so the test results are unreliable
All inoculated cultures grew well, so the control turbidity is a harmless artefact
The control tube shows the broth is nutrient-rich, which validates the test growth
The isolates are fast-growing and grow in the control by design, so the test is still valid

rubric: Growth in a sterility control means contamination, invalidating the experiment.
Distractors rationalize the control as acceptable.

items.prompt: E. coli grows in medium with glucose and lactose. It grows, stops for a lag period, then grows again more slowly. What best explains the lag?

options.label: Lactose cannot enter cells until the cells have completed another round of DNA replication
Glucose repressed the lac operon until it ran out, so lactose enzymes were made late
Lactose is toxic, so most cells die back before the resistant survivors resume growth
The cells entered death phase, and a later mutation let survivors use lactose as fuel

rubric: Diauxic growth reflects catabolite repression: glucose is used first, then lac enzymes are made.
Distractors invent toxicity or mutation instead of regulation.

items.prompt: A 4-day-old Bacillus culture is Gram stained and many cells appear pink although the species is Gram-positive. Which is the most likely cause?

options.label: Autolysis in old cells damages the walls, so they lose crystal violet when decolorized
Safranin was applied too briefly, so the Gram-positive cells took up the counterstain only weakly
Crystal violet cannot bind peptidoglycan in cells of that species, so no primary stain is retained
The cells gained an outer membrane as the culture aged, so the decolorizer removed the stain

rubric: Gram-positive cells in aged cultures often lose wall integrity and appear gram-variable or negative.
Distractors blame procedure or invent structural changes.

items.prompt: Donor and recipient bacteria are in the two arms of a U-tube separated by a filter that blocks cells but passes DNA and phage. Resistance transfers only when cells are mixed directly, and DNase does not prevent it. Which mechanism?

options.label: Transformation, uptake of free DNA from the medium
Vertical transfer of resistance genes during binary fission
Generalised transduction, DNA carried by bacteriophage
Conjugation through a pilus-mediated bridge

rubric: Transfer needs contact and is DNase-resistant, which indicates conjugation.
Transformation and transduction would cross the filter, and DNase would block free DNA.

items.prompt: A lysogenic E. coli culture is stable until exposed to UV light, then lyses within an hour although no phage were added. Which explanation is best?

options.label: UV light mutated the cells into a form that makes lysozyme
UV light converted the bacterial ribosomes into phage capsids
UV damage triggered induction of a resident prophage into the lytic cycle
UV light contaminated the culture with environmental phage particles

rubric: DNA damage activates the SOS response and induces the prophage.
Distractors ignore the pre-existing prophage.

items.prompt: A disk diffusion plate shows no zone of inhibition around an antibiotic disk, though the organism is known to be susceptible. Which could explain this? Select all that apply.

options.label: The agar was poured far thicker than standard
The disk was expired and had lost potency
The agar was poured thinner than standard
The plate was incubated for the standard 18 hours
The inoculum was much denser than standard

rubric: Expired drug, heavy inoculum and thick agar all reduce or hide zones.
Thin agar enlarges zones and standard incubation is correct.

items.prompt: A patient with a urinary infection failed ampicillin therapy. The isolate is a Gram-negative rod, colourless on MacConkey, oxidase-positive and produces green pigment. Which explanation best accounts for the treatment failure?

options.label: Lactose fermentation produces acid that inactivates the drug in the urine
Lack of a peptidoglycan cell wall, so the beta-lactam has no target
A thick Gram-positive peptidoglycan wall that blocks the drug entering
Intrinsic resistance from low outer-membrane permeability and efflux

rubric: The profile fits Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which is intrinsically resistant to many beta-lactams via permeability and efflux.
Distractors give wrong structural or metabolic reasons.

items.prompt: An E. coli isolate grows in the presence of ampicillin alone but is inhibited by ampicillin combined with clavulanate. Which interpretation best explains this result?

options.label: It has an efflux pump that clavulanate blocks, which lets ampicillin build up inside
It has altered penicillin-binding proteins that clavulanate repairs, which restores drug binding
It lacks a cell wall, so clavulanate adds a second target that ampicillin cannot reach
It makes a beta-lactamase that clavulanate inhibits, which restores ampicillin activity

rubric: Clavulanate is a beta-lactamase inhibitor, so rescue of ampicillin points to enzymatic hydrolysis as the resistance mechanism.
Distractors confuse target alteration or efflux with enzymatic inactivation.

items.prompt: A culture in medium containing both glucose and lactose grows quickly, pauses, then resumes at a slower rate. What best explains the pause?

options.label: Acid from glucose fermentation halts growth until the cells use lactose products to buffer the medium
Lactose is toxic until glucose is gone, so cells wait while they build a detoxifying enzyme to cope
Glucose runs out, repression lifts, and lac enzymes must be induced before lactose is used
Cells fall out of synchrony once glucose runs out, so turbidity stops rising until division resumes evenly

rubric: Diauxic growth reflects preferential glucose use, then a lag while the lac operon is induced once repression is relieved.
Distractors give non-regulatory explanations such as pH change or toxicity.

items.prompt: A Geobacillus stearothermophilus spore indicator grew after an autoclave cycle where the chamber gauge read 121 °C for 30 minutes. The load was densely packed bags of dry media. What is the most likely cause?

options.label: Trapped air blocked steam from the load core, so the core never reached sterilizing conditions
The spores were killed, but vegetative cells contaminated the indicator's recovery medium
Moist heat at 121 °C is below the minimum temperature that can kill any bacterial spore
Steam kills by dehydration, and the dense dry load prevented the needed water loss

rubric: Air pockets in dense loads stop steam penetration, so the chamber reading does not reflect the temperature at the core.
Distractors misstate how moist heat kills or blame contamination without evidence.

items.prompt: A known Gram-positive Bacillus subtilis culture from a 3-day-old plate stains mostly pink on Gram stain. What best explains this?

options.label: Old cultures overproduce teichoic acid, which blocks crystal violet from entering the cell
Over-incubated plates deplete cell lipids, so alcohol cannot enter and the counterstain dominates
Old cells gain an outer membrane that holds the safranin counterstain more strongly
Aging cells have damaged walls that no longer retain the crystal violet–iodine complex after decolorizing

rubric: Cells in old cultures can lose wall integrity and fail to retain the crystal violet complex, so they appear falsely Gram-negative.
Distractors invent structural changes that Bacillus does not undergo.

items.prompt: A non-toxigenic Corynebacterium diphtheriae strain starts making toxin after exposure to a phage lysate. DNase treatment of the lysate has no effect, and no donor cells are present. Which process explains this?

options.label: Conjugation, in which a pilus carries a plasmid from a living donor into the recipient
Lysogenic conversion, in which a temperate phage integrates and brings in the toxin gene
Transformation, in which recipient cells take up naked DNA released from lysed donor cells
Spontaneous mutation, in which a point change switches on a silent toxin gene by chance

rubric: DNase resistance and absence of donors point to phage-borne DNA, so a temperate phage carrying tox causes lysogenic conversion.
Transformation would be blocked by DNase, and conjugation needs living donors.

items.prompt: A patient on antibiotics for 3 days has a positive PCR for a bacterial pathogen in sputum but a negative culture. Which explanations are plausible? Select all that apply.

options.label: The organism may be fastidious and unable to grow on the medium used
PCR amplifies only DNA from metabolically active cells, so it overestimates live counts
PCR can detect DNA from cells already killed by the antibiotic
A negative culture shows the primers amplified human DNA, not bacterial DNA
Antibiotic carried over in the specimen may suppress growth on the plate

rubric: Nucleic acid persists after death, fastidious organisms miss culture, and drug carryover inhibits growth, so all three explain the discrepancy.
PCR does not select for live cells, and a negative culture says nothing about primer specificity.

items.prompt: Cases of C. difficile diarrhoea keep rising on a ward after staff switched to alcohol-based hand rub for all hand hygiene. Most patients recently received clindamycin. Which analysis best explains continued spread?

options.label: Alcohol rub fails on Gram-positive rods because thick peptidoglycan blocks the alcohol from entering
Clindamycin residues on staff hands neutralise the alcohol and shorten the effective contact time
Alcohol does not inactivate spores, so hands stay contaminated and soap-and-water washing is needed
Alcohol rub selects for toxin-producing strains, which then outcompete non-toxigenic ones on hands

rubric: C. difficile forms spores that resist alcohol, and washing physically removes them.
Distractors blame selection, wall structure or drug residues, none of which explain alcohol failure.

items.prompt: A heat-sensitive flexible endoscope must be reprocessed between patients. Criteria: kill bacterial spores, avoid damaging the scope, and finish within a few hours. Which option is best?

options.label: Autoclave at 121 °C, because steam is the most reliable sporicide and leaves no chemical residue
Use peracetic acid sterilant for its labelled contact time, because it is sporicidal at low temperature
Wipe with a quaternary ammonium disinfectant, because it is non-corrosive and leaves residual activity
Soak in 70% ethanol for 10 minutes, because it rapidly kills vegetative bacteria and evaporates cleanly

rubric: Peracetic acid is sporicidal without heat, so it meets all three criteria.
Ethanol and quaternary ammonium compounds are not reliably sporicidal, and autoclaving damages heat-sensitive scopes.

items.prompt: A team says a new compound is bactericidal against S. aureus because its MIC is very low (0.5 µg/mL). Which critique is most valid?

options.label: The claim is sound, because any compound that stops growth at a low dose must also be lethal
MIC shows only inhibited growth, so an MBC or time-kill assay is needed to claim killing
MIC can only be read for Gram-negative bacteria, so the test is invalid for S. aureus
A low MIC shows the compound is bacteriostatic, because killing always needs much higher doses

rubric: MIC measures inhibition, not killing, so bactericidal activity needs MBC or time-kill data.
Distractors wrongly equate MIC with static or cidal action, or restrict MIC to one Gram group.

items.prompt: Home canners want to store low-acid green beans (pH about 5.5) for a year at room temperature. Criteria: eliminate C. botulinum spores and be reproducible. Which method is best?

options.label: Hot-filling jars and inverting them, because the heat of filling seals out spores that could germinate
Pressure canning at about 116–121 °C, because only temperatures above 100 °C reliably destroy spores
Boiling-water bath for 3 hours, because the long exposure compensates for the lower temperature
Adding 2% salt before a water bath, because salt halts germination of all spores at room temperature

rubric: Spores survive 100 °C, so pressure canning is needed to reach lethal temperatures in low-acid food.
Distractors rely on time, filling heat or salt, none of which reliably destroy C. botulinum spores.

items.prompt: A student concludes an isolate is an obligate anaerobe because it grew only in a sealed jar and not on plates in an ambient incubator. Which critique is strongest?

options.label: The result is conclusive, because any organism failing to grow in air must lack catalase and so be anaerobic
Obligate anaerobes die in sealed jars, so growth there suggests the isolate tolerates oxygen
Jars always hold residual oxygen, so growth there can only come from facultative anaerobes
Jars also differ in CO2 level, so a capnophile could give this result; test with CO2 incubation and aerotolerance

rubric: Anaerobic jars change CO2 as well as O2, so the design confounds the variables; a controlled comparison is needed.
Distractors misstate jar conditions or treat catalase absence as proof.

items.prompt: A cell culture supplement contains heat-labile vitamins and must be free of bacteria and fungi. Viruses are not a concern. Which method best meets these criteria?

options.label: Filter through a 0.22 µm membrane, because the pores retain bacteria and fungi
Filter through a 0.45 µm membrane, because that pore size retains every bacterial cell
Expose to UV light for 30 minutes, because UV penetrates liquids and sterilises evenly
Autoclave at 121 °C for 15 minutes, because pressurised steam kills all microbes reliably

rubric: A 0.22 µm filter removes bacteria and fungi and spares heat-labile components.
Autoclaving destroys vitamins, UV penetrates liquids poorly, and 0.45 µm filters can pass small bacteria.

items.prompt: A lab will test whether a new alcohol hand sanitizer reduces bacterial load on skin. Which design features make the conclusion more valid? Select all that apply.

options.label: Include a placebo control applied in the same way
Apply the product to sterile glass slides only and infer skin efficacy
Add a neutralizer to the recovery fluid so residual alcohol does not keep killing cells
Count colonies on one agar plate from a single volunteer and extrapolate
Replicate across several volunteers with randomised order of products

rubric: Controls, neutralization of carryover and replication each reduce bias or false effects.
Single-sample counts and inert surfaces do not represent skin use or variation.

items.prompt: A hospital must choose how to screen admissions for MRSA. Criteria: positive patients isolated within hours, and positives need an isolate for susceptibility testing. Culture takes 48 hours. PCR takes 2 hours but yields no isolate. Which strategy is best?

options.label: Culture first, then run PCR after 48 hours to confirm the negative results
PCR on admission, then culture only the PCR-positive samples to obtain isolates
PCR alone, since speed is the only criterion that really matters here
Culture all admissions alone, since every positive then comes with an isolate

rubric: PCR gives fast isolation decisions and culturing positives supplies isolates, so both criteria are met.
Culture alone is too slow, PCR alone gives no isolate, and delayed PCR defeats the purpose.

items.prompt: A lab reports that drug A gave a 24 mm inhibition zone and drug B a 16 mm zone against the same isolate by disk diffusion. It concludes A is more potent and should be preferred. Which critique best undermines this conclusion?

options.label: Zone size depends on diffusion rate and drug-specific breakpoints, so diameters can't be compared across drugs
Disk diffusion is validated mainly for Gram-negative isolates, so neither zone is reliably interpretable for this organism
Zone diameters are read at a standard incubation time, and an early reading would make both zone values unreliable here
A larger zone usually reflects bacteriostatic action rather than killing, so drug A may be the weaker choice in severe infection

rubric: Breakpoints are drug-specific and zone size reflects diffusion as well as potency, so cross-drug comparison of diameters is invalid.
Distractors invent absolute rules about Gram status, incubation time or static action that do not exist.

items.prompt: Neurosurgical instruments were used on a patient with suspected Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease. Criteria: prion infectivity must be reduced as far as possible, and the instruments tolerate NaOH and steam. Which reprocessing is best supported?

options.label: Wipe with 70% ethanol and air dry, since alcohol denatures proteins and prions are simple proteins that lack any protective structure
Soak in 1 N NaOH, then autoclave at 134 °C, since prions resist routine sterilisation but alkali plus hot steam degrades them
Expose to ethylene oxide gas overnight, since the gas penetrates crevices and alkylates the nucleic acid of the infectious agent
Autoclave at 121 °C for 15 minutes, since this standard cycle kills bacterial spores and so must also inactivate prions

rubric: Prions are unusually resistant; NaOH combined with 134 °C steam is the accepted high-level approach.
Distractors assume spore-killing cycles, alcohol or nucleic-acid-targeting gas work, ignoring that prions lack nucleic acid and resist standard methods.

items.prompt: A batch culture's OD600 stays constant for 48 h after exponential growth ends. A student concludes the population is stable and fully viable. Which judgement is best?

options.label: Unsupported: turbidity also counts dead cells and debris, so viable plate counts are needed to judge survival
Supported: stationary-phase cells are metabolically inert, so a constant OD confirms they all remain viable
Unsupported: OD600 is valid only during exponential phase, so it cannot be read once growth slows
Supported: constant turbidity means birth and death rates are equal, which proves the cells present are healthy

rubric: Optical density measures light scattering by all particles, living or dead, so viability needs a separate assay.
Distractors treat OD as a viability measure or wrongly restrict its validity to exponential phase.

items.prompt: Chlorinated water must be tested for Vibrio cholerae that may be viable but non-culturable. Criteria: count only cells with intact membranes, and give a result within one day. Which method is best?

options.label: PMA-treated qPCR, since the dye blocks DNA from membrane-damaged cells so only intact cells amplify
Standard qPCR on extracted DNA, since a positive signal shows intact living cells
Gram stain microscopy of the concentrate, since stained cells are intact and identifiable to species
Selective agar plating for 48 hours, since colonies prove the cells were alive

rubric: Propidium monoazide excludes DNA from dead cells, and qPCR is rapid and independent of culturability.
Plating misses VBNC cells and is slow; plain qPCR detects dead-cell DNA; Gram stain cannot confirm species or viability.

items.prompt: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella appears on five hospital wards. Which finding would most strongly support horizontal plasmid spread rather than clonal expansion of a single strain?

options.label: One carbapenemase gene on near-identical plasmids in unrelated sequence types
Resistant isolates came only from the intensive care unit, where antibiotic use is highest and selection pressure is strongest
Isolates are all carbapenem resistant but differ in susceptibility to several unrelated drug classes, such as aminoglycosides
Isolates share one MLST type and PFGE pattern, with the resistance gene on the chromosome

rubric: A shared mobile element across genetically unrelated hosts indicates horizontal transfer.
Distractors describe clonal spread or selection pressure, which do not discriminate between the two mechanisms.

items.prompt: A report says 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing found no reads of pathogen X, so a stool sample is pathogen-free. Which criticisms are valid? Select all that apply.

options.label: 16S sequencing cannot detect bacteria that fail to grow in culture
Primer bias can under-amplify certain taxa
A short 16S region often cannot resolve species within some genera
16S amplicons detect viruses and fungi, so absence of X is impossible
Reads below the detection limit do not prove the organism is absent

rubric: Detection limits, limited resolution and primer bias all weaken a negative claim from 16S data.
16S primers do not target viruses, and sequencing is culture-independent, so the other options are false.

items.prompt: A plant canning low-acid vegetables finds a few swollen cans with gas and a sour odour. Isolates are Gram-positive spore-forming rods. Records show retort time was shortened last month to save energy. Which is the best-judged priority?

options.label: Revalidate the retort cycle's lethality at the can's slowest-heating point, since surviving spores are the likely cause
Add a surfactant and chlorine pre-wash for raw vegetables, since a lower starting microbial load removes the need to revalidate the cycle
Increase chlorine in the cooling water only, since post-process leakage of vegetative cells through the seams is the likely cause
Move finished cans to 4 °C storage, since refrigeration will inactivate any spores that survived the shortened process

rubric: Spore-formers plus a shortened thermal process point to inadequate lethality at the cold spot.
Distractors target leakage, load reduction or cold storage, none of which fixes or kills surviving spores.

items.prompt: After mutagenesis of a prototrophic bacterium you must enrich for auxotrophic mutants before screening. Which plan fits these needs?

options.label: Plate directly on minimal medium, pick the smallest colonies, and replica-plate them to rich medium to confirm that they are auxotrophs
Grow in minimal medium with penicillin, wash, plate on rich medium, then replica-plate to minimal; prototrophs lyse, auxotrophs survive
Grow in minimal medium without antibiotic for several generations, then plate on rich medium; auxotrophs gradually outgrow prototrophs using stores
Grow in rich medium with penicillin, wash, then plate on rich medium and replica-plate to minimal; all cells divide, so auxotrophs die least

rubric: Penicillin kills only growing cells, so in minimal medium it removes prototrophs and enriches non-growing auxotrophs.
Distractors ignore that auxotrophs cannot grow on minimal medium or that penicillin needs growth to act.

items.prompt: Design an enrichment for sulfate-reducing bacteria from marsh mud. They are strict anaerobes that use sulfate as terminal electron acceptor and are outcompeted by nitrate reducers. Which medium and conditions fit?

options.label: Anoxic medium with acetate and nitrate, since nitrate boosts respiration of all anaerobes
Anoxic reduced medium with lactate and sulfate, no nitrate, in a sealed dark bottle
Aerobic medium with sulfate and thiosulfate under a lamp, since sulfur compounds select for the target
Aerated glucose medium with nitrate, shaken at 37 °C, since fast growth enriches the target

rubric: Anoxia, an electron donor, sulfate as acceptor and no nitrate select for sulfate reducers.
Distractors allow oxygen or provide nitrate, which favours competitors.

items.prompt: Design a vaccine against an encapsulated bacterium for infants under 2 years. Constraints: polysaccharides alone give a poor T-independent response at this age, no live organism may be used, and immune memory is required. Which design meets all?

options.label: Free carrier protein mixed with unlinked capsular polysaccharide, since both antigens are in the same injection and reach the same B cells
Heat-killed whole bacteria without adjuvant, since killed cells reliably give T-dependent memory in infants
Purified capsular polysaccharide alone at a higher dose, repeated monthly to drive memory B cells
Capsular polysaccharide covalently linked to a carrier protein, recruiting T-helper cells for memory

rubric: Conjugation lets B cells that bind polysaccharide receive T-cell help from carrier peptides, giving memory in infants.
Unlinked mixtures or polysaccharide alone remain T-independent; killed cells without adjuvant are weak.

items.prompt: Design an experiment showing that gene transfer between two bacterial strains occurs by transduction rather than conjugation or transformation. Which setup does this?

options.label: U-tube with a 0.45 µm filter and no DNase; transfer across the filter shows the agent is a phage, since cells cannot pass
Direct mixing on a membrane with DNase added; transfer still occurring shows the agent is a phage, since free DNA is destroyed
U-tube with a 0.45 µm filter and DNase; transfer still occurring shows a DNase-resistant agent
U-tube with a 0.02 µm filter and no DNase; transfer still occurring shows the agent is a phage, since cells cannot pass

rubric: The filter blocks cell contact while passing phage, and DNase removes free DNA, so surviving transfer implicates phage.
Distractors use a pore size that blocks phage, allow conjugation, or leave transformation unexcluded.

items.prompt: Design a phage preparation to treat a multidrug-resistant infection. Constraints: resistance must be slow to emerge, phage must not transfer genes to the host, and no toxin genes may be delivered. Which design fits?

options.label: One temperate phage at very high titre, since lysogeny gives lasting protection against the host
Three lytic phages that all use one outer-membrane receptor, so a single mutation is unlikely
Several strictly lytic phages binding different receptors, screened to lack integrase and toxin genes
Phages chosen for widest host range regardless of lifestyle, since genome screening adds delay but no safety

rubric: Different receptors slow resistance, and lytic, genome-screened phages avoid lysogeny and toxin transfer.
Temperate phages risk lysogeny, and shared receptors let one mutation defeat the whole mixture.

items.prompt: You must validate a new autoclave cycle for a dense mixed load. Which elements belong in a sound validation plan? Select all that apply.

options.label: E. coli suspension indicators, because it is the most heat-resistant common organism
A pressure gauge reading alone, since pressure fixes temperature in steam
Geobacillus stearothermophilus spore indicators at the hardest-to-heat locations in the load
Repeat runs with worst-case load configurations such as maximum density
Thermocouples inside the load to document time at temperature

rubric: Resistant spore indicators, in-load temperature data and worst-case repeats together show sterilising conditions are reached.
E. coli is heat-labile, and pressure alone misses trapped air and cold spots.

items.prompt: A team engineers a probiotic E. coli for gut delivery. Constraints: it must not persist outside the host, must carry no antibiotic resistance marker in the final strain, and must not depend on a plasmid that could transfer. Which containment design meets all three?

options.label: Chromosomal essential gene redesigned to need a synthetic amino acid, with markerless edits
Chromosomal deletion of thyA, since thymidine is absent everywhere outside the host
Plasmid-encoded toxin-antitoxin kill switch maintained by an ampicillin resistance gene
Slowing growth by deleting a metabolic gene so the strain is outcompeted in the environment

rubric: Dependence on a synthetic nutrient confines growth, and chromosomal markerless edits satisfy the marker and plasmid constraints.
Distractors use a plasmid with a marker, an auxotrophy rescued by environmental thymidine, or mere attenuation.
